svg.text: Each of the six answers below is one shaded region of the same 13-by-4 grid. Face-values are
columns, suits are rows; a card is one cell, named by exactly one column and one row.
all hearts, plus the other three aces
TWO PARTITIONS, CROSSING EACH OTHER PERFECTLY
The 13 face-value sets partition the deck into blocks of 4; the 4 suit sets partition it into blocks
of 13. Both verified. And every face-value meets every suit in exactly one card — also verified.
That single fact decides every part: two sets of the same kind are disjoint, which is part e, while
two of different kinds always meet in one card, which is parts a and d.
The correction term is the size of the intersection — one card in the first case, none in the second.
Both counts confirmed by listing the cards, as is |A ∪ ♡ ∪ K| = 4+13+4 − 1 − 0 − 1 + 0 = 19.
